text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own. Men dominate senior panels in most ministries, so it happens constantly in appointments where sex played no role. Treated as your main argument, it looks weak and puts the panel on the defensive.

It does have value as context — it can support a claim that the process lacked safeguards, and in some jurisdictions balanced panels are required or recommended by guidelines. Check yours.

Your strongest point is the two-week silence on a written explanation, to which you are likely entitled. Chase that first, in writing, with a deadline. Compare the stated criteria against both profiles. Then decide whether a pattern exists worth naming.
